sections.h2: Which rental rules apply when you sell
sections.html:
Four sets of rules matter most: the security deposit statute, the notice rules for ending a tenancy, the limits on landlord entry, and the eviction procedure. All of them sit in chapter 47-16 and chapter 47-32 of the North Dakota Century Code. A landlord who plans to sell a house with a tenant in it needs to handle each one correctly, whether the buyer wants the tenant to stay or wants a vacant house.

This guide summarizes the statutes. It is general information and not legal advice, so a landlord with a dispute in progress should talk to a North Dakota attorney.

Under section 47-16-07.1, a landlord may generally collect a deposit of up to one month's rent, and must hold it in a federally insured, interest-bearing account for the tenant's benefit. The deductions and the return deadline are tightly set, and getting them wrong can cost a landlord triple the amount wrongly kept.

North Dakota security deposit rules
TopicRule
Deposit capOne month's rent, with exceptions for a tenant with a felony conviction or a prior judgment for violating a rental agreement
Pet depositNo more than the greater of $2,500 or two months' rent; not for service or companion animals
Return deadlineItemized deductions and any balance within 30 days after the lease ends and possession is delivered
InterestNot required if the tenant lived there less than nine months
Wrongful withholdingExposes the landlord to treble damages

Deductions may cover damage or unpaid rent but not normal wear and tear. When a rental is sold, the deposit is a liability that has to be dealt with in the closing paperwork, so ask your title company how the deposit and interest will move to the new owner.

The landlord must give the tenant a written statement describing the property's facilities and condition when the rental agreement begins, and both parties sign it. Under N.D.C.C. 47-16-07.2 it serves as prima facie proof of the condition on that date.

Tenants should check the report before signing, because a tenant is presumed responsible for damage that is not listed. For a landlord preparing to sell, the signed statement is also the best record of what the house looked like when the tenant arrived. Keep a copy with the lease so a buyer and the title company can see it.

A landlord may enter at reasonable hours and in a reasonable manner for listed purposes, and showings to purchasers are among them. Section 47-16-07.3 also allows entry at any time in an emergency, or when the landlord reasonably believes the tenant has abandoned the unit or is in substantial violation of the lease.

  • Unless it is impractical, the landlord must notify the tenant and ask for consent that identifies a specific time.
  • Consent cannot be unreasonably withheld, and it is presumed if the tenant does not object after notice of a time certain.
  • Using access rights to harass or intimidate a tenant is prohibited.

Plan showings around the tenant's schedule and put the notice in writing. A string of unannounced visits can turn a cooperative tenant into a difficult one.

sections.h2: Ending a tenancy when the landlord sells
sections.html:
Selling a house does not by itself end a lease, so the way to end a tenancy depends on the type of tenancy. For a month-to-month tenancy, either side can end it with at least one calendar month's written notice given at any time, and rent is due through the termination date. For a tenancy with no stated term, notice must be at least as long as the lease period, up to one calendar month.

A landlord who wants to change the terms of a month-to-month tenancy must give written notice at least 30 days before the end of the month, and the change takes effect if the tenant stays. A tenant who does not accept the change may end the tenancy at the end of the month with at least 25 days' notice.

A lease that requires notice longer than one month must say so and include a space for the tenant's initials. Without the initials, the tenant may end the tenancy on the last day of a month with one calendar month's notice.

sections.h2: What a landlord must keep in working order
sections.html:
A residential landlord must follow the building and housing codes that materially affect health and safety, keep the unit fit and habitable, and keep common areas clean and safe. Section 47-16-13.1 also requires waste removal, running water, reasonable hot water and reasonable heat, with listed exceptions, and the landlord gets a reasonable time to fix a problem after being told.

Tenants carry duties too under 47-16-13.2: keep their area clean and safe, dispose of waste, avoid damaging the premises, and avoid disturbing neighbors. A tenant may end the lease early under 47-16-17 if the landlord fails to make repairs within a reasonable time after a request, and a landlord may end it under 47-16-16 if the tenant uses the property contrary to the agreement.

The Attorney General's office does not take complaints about landlord and tenant disputes or mediate them. Tenants can turn to Legal Services of North Dakota, a private attorney or small claims court, and discrimination complaints go to the North Dakota Department of Labor.

Eviction in North Dakota is a court action, and a landlord cannot remove a tenant without a court order from a district court. The grounds are listed in N.D.C.C. 47-32-01, and the main ones for a rental follow.

  • Holding over after the lease ends, or failing to pay rent within three days after it is due.
  • Unreasonably disturbing other tenants' peaceful enjoyment.
  • Materially violating the written lease.
  • Remaining after a foreclosure sale, deed or cancelled contract for deed once the redemption time has expired.

For holdover, nonpayment, foreclosure-related and lease-violation cases the landlord must give three days' written notice of intent to evict before filing. The court summons sets an appearance date between 3 and 15 days after it is issued. If the landlord wins, the judgment is for immediate restitution of the premises, although the court may stay enforcement up to five days when immediate removal would cause substantial hardship.

A landlord may not lock a tenant out, cut off utilities or take belongings. If an LLC or corporation owns the property, the court's published self-help forms cannot be used, and the entity must be represented by a lawyer admitted in North Dakota.

A claim for accrued rent and damages can be joined with the eviction action, but other claims generally cannot, and a tenant's counterclaims are limited to setoffs against rent or damages. Section 47-32-05 lets a person move to seal an eviction record for nonpayment or property damage seven years after the order is satisfied, if there has been no other eviction in that time.

Back rent and damages are tied to the landlord's own claim against the tenant, so a landlord who sells should settle in the sale contract who keeps the right to collect them.

A short checklist keeps a rental sale clean.

  • Pull the lease, the move-in condition statement and the deposit records.
  • Confirm the deposit is in a federally insured, interest-bearing account and decide how it will transfer.
  • Give written notice before every showing and ask for a specific time.
  • If the buyer wants the house vacant, use the notice rules for the tenancy type, and file for eviction only on a statutory ground.
  • Keep rent payment methods open: a landlord may not charge a fee for accepting cash, a check or a money order for rent.

Tell any buyer up front whether the tenant will stay, because that decides which notice rules apply and how long the process takes. A cash buyer who takes the house with the tenant in place can spare you the notice periods, but the deposit still has to be accounted for at closing.

faqs.q: How much can a landlord charge for a security deposit?
faqs.a: A landlord can generally charge up to one month's rent. Higher limits apply to a tenant with a felony conviction or a prior judgment for violating a rental agreement, and pet deposits are capped separately at the greater of $2,500 or two months' rent.

faqs.q: How long does a landlord have to return a deposit?
faqs.a: Thirty days. The landlord must deliver an itemized list of deductions and any balance within 30 days after the lease ends and the tenant gives up possession.

faqs.q: How much notice ends a month-to-month tenancy?
faqs.a: At least one calendar month's written notice, from either the landlord or the tenant, given at any time.

faqs.q: Can a landlord show the house to buyers while it is rented?
faqs.a: Yes, within reason. Entry for showings must be at reasonable hours and in a reasonable manner, and the landlord must notify the tenant and seek consent for a specific time unless that is impractical.

faqs.q: Can a landlord evict a tenant without going to court?
faqs.a: No. A tenant cannot be evicted without a court order from a North Dakota district court, and lockouts, utility shutoffs and taking belongings are not allowed.
